1. Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended) — highest authority and the constitutional framework for public finance.
2. Finance (Control and Management) Act, 1958 (cited in the Financial Regulations as Cap. 144, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria 1990) — primary legislation for federal financial control and accounting.
3. Annual and supplementary Appropriation Acts — primary legislation authorising the expenditure to which they relate; the retrieved excerpts identify these categories but give no particular Act or year.
4. Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2007 — primary legislation in the fiscal-responsibility framework.
5. Public Procurement Act, 2007 — primary legislation governing public procurement.
6. Financial Reporting Council Act, 2011 — primary legislation relevant to financial reporting and accountability.
7. Pension Reform Act, 2014 (as amended) — primary legislation relevant to pension finances.
8. Finance Act, 2022 — primary legislation identified in the evidence as supporting fiscal-consolidation measures.
9. Federal Government Financial Regulations (revised October 2009) — lower-tier rules for federal financial administration, beneath the Constitution and Acts.
10. Treasury Circulars — administrative instructions below Acts and Financial Regulations (inferred hierarchical placement). A cited 2024 Public Finance Management Bill discusses their application, but its enactment is not established; that Bill is therefore not listed as a law in force.
